summary: Modern data platforms increasingly embed AI/ML capabilities directly into the database layer, allowing SQL-native model inference, LLM access, embedding generation, and vector similarity search without moving data to separate systems. The vector database market is growing rapidly (projected to reach ~$17.9B by 2034 at a ~24% CAGR), and Gartner projects 30% of enterprises will rely on vector-based retrieval for GenAI by 2026. Approaches vary: some platforms offer fully managed, native vector search and LLM functions (Snowflake Cortex, Databricks, MongoDB Atlas), while others provide ML inference via integration with external model services (Aurora ML, Redshift ML) or rely on extensions (PostgreSQL pgvector).

databases.name: Snowflake (Cortex AI)
databases.ai_feature: Cortex AI — fully managed LLM and ML functions in SQL
databases.description: Snowflake Cortex provides serverless, SQL- and Python-callable AI functions including LLM access (COMPLETE, SUMMARIZE, TRANSLATE, SENTIMENT, EXTRACT_ANSWER), embedding generation (EMBED_TEXT), Cortex Search for RAG, Cortex Analyst for natural-language-to-SQL, and Cortex Agents. Cortex is also exposed to Snowflake Postgres, letting Postgres workloads call Cortex AI functions.
databases.vector_search_notes: Native. Snowflake supports a built-in VECTOR data type with VECTOR_COSINE_SIMILARITY / VECTOR_L2_DISTANCE functions, plus the managed Cortex Search service for hybrid semantic retrieval. Snowflake Postgres can also store and query vectors.
databases.llm_integration: Native hosted LLMs (e.g., Llama, Mistral, Claude via Cortex) accessible through SQL/Python functions; no external API keys required for managed models.
databases.pricing_notes: Consumption-based, billed in Snowflake credits by tokens processed or compute consumed per Cortex function; serverless with no infrastructure to manage.

databases.name: Google BigQuery (BigQuery ML + Vertex AI)
databases.ai_feature: BigQuery ML with Vertex AI and Gemini integration
databases.description: BigQuery ML lets users create and run ML models (regression, classification, clustering, time series, etc.) using SQL. It integrates with Vertex AI to call hosted foundation models (Gemini) via ML.GENERATE_TEXT, ML.GENERATE_EMBEDDING, and remote model endpoints, enabling text generation, summarization, and embeddings directly in SQL.
databases.vector_search_notes: Native. BigQuery supports a VECTOR data type with VECTOR_SEARCH function and vector indexes (IVF/TreeAH) for approximate nearest-neighbor search over embeddings.
databases.llm_integration: Deep integration with Vertex AI and Gemini models via remote models and ML.GENERATE_* functions; also supports connecting to custom Vertex endpoints.
databases.pricing_notes: Billed by bytes processed (on-demand) or slot-based capacity; LLM/embedding calls incur Vertex AI inference charges in addition to BigQuery query costs.

databases.name: PostgreSQL (pgvector + pgai)
databases.ai_feature: pgvector extension for embeddings + pgai for in-database AI workflows
databases.description: pgvector adds vector storage and similarity search to PostgreSQL, while pgai (from Timescale) adds helper functions to generate embeddings and call LLM providers (OpenAI, Ollama, etc.) directly from SQL, and pgvectorscale improves ANN performance. Together they turn vanilla Postgres into a RAG-capable store.
databases.vector_search_notes: Native-via-extension. Core PostgreSQL has no built-in vector search; pgvector is a widely adopted open-source extension installed into Postgres providing the vector type, HNSW/IVFFlat indexes, and distance operators. Considered standard on self-managed and most managed Postgres.
databases.llm_integration: Via pgai, Postgres can call external LLM/embedding APIs (OpenAI, Anthropic, Cohere, Ollama, Vertex) from SQL; otherwise integration is handled in the application layer with LangChain, etc.
databases.pricing_notes: Open source and free; costs are just the underlying Postgres compute/storage (self-hosted or managed) plus any external LLM API usage fees.

databases.name: Amazon Aurora ML
databases.ai_feature: Aurora Machine Learning — SQL integration with SageMaker and Bedrock
databases.description: Aurora ML lets you call machine learning models directly from SQL queries by integrating with Amazon SageMaker (custom models), Amazon Bedrock (foundation models/LLMs), and Amazon Comprehend (NLP). You add ML predictions, text generation, and sentiment analysis to queries without writing application code.
databases.vector_search_notes: Not natively built into Aurora ML. Vector search on Aurora PostgreSQL is available only through the pgvector extension (a third-party/open-source extension), not as a native Aurora ML feature. Aurora ML itself is about model inference, not vector storage.
databases.llm_integration: Integrates with Amazon Bedrock foundation models and SageMaker-hosted models invoked from SQL functions; LLM text generation available via aws_bedrock SQL functions.
databases.pricing_notes: No separate Aurora ML charge; you pay for the underlying Aurora cluster plus the SageMaker/Bedrock/Comprehend inference requests consumed.

databases.name: Amazon Redshift ML
databases.ai_feature: Redshift ML — create and run ML models with SQL via SageMaker
databases.description: Redshift ML enables analysts to create, train, and deploy ML models using the CREATE MODEL SQL command, which automatically leverages Amazon SageMaker Autopilot behind the scenes. It supports in-database prediction (inference) and integrates with Bedrock for generative AI functions directly in the data warehouse.
databases.vector_search_notes: Not natively supported as part of Redshift ML. Redshift does not offer general-purpose native vector similarity search; it is primarily a prediction/inference service. (Preview features and workarounds exist, but there is no mature built-in vector search comparable to native vector databases.)
databases.llm_integration: Integrates with Amazon Bedrock for generative AI and SageMaker for custom/LLM models, invokable from SQL; supports BYO SageMaker endpoints for remote inference.
databases.pricing_notes: No additional Redshift ML charge for in-Redshift inference beyond cluster costs; model training uses SageMaker resources and Bedrock/remote inference is billed separately.

databases.name: Databricks (Mosaic AI + Vector Search)
databases.ai_feature: Mosaic AI platform with managed Vector Search
databases.description: Databricks Mosaic AI provides end-to-end GenAI tooling: model serving, foundation model APIs, fine-tuning, agent framework, and evaluation, all integrated with Unity Catalog governance. Mosaic AI Vector Search is a managed vector database that automatically syncs and indexes embeddings from Delta tables for semantic and RAG retrieval.
databases.vector_search_notes: Native. Mosaic AI Vector Search is a first-party managed vector database with automatic Delta table sync, managed embedding computation, and hybrid (keyword + semantic) search.
databases.llm_integration: Native Foundation Model APIs and external model serving (OpenAI, Anthropic, etc.) plus fine-tuning and agent tooling via Mosaic AI; LLMs callable from SQL (ai_query) and notebooks.
databases.pricing_notes: Consumption-based using Databricks Units (DBUs); Vector Search and model serving billed by compute/endpoint usage plus storage; foundation model APIs billed per token or provisioned throughput.

databases.name: MongoDB Atlas Vector Search
databases.ai_feature: Atlas Vector Search — native vector search in the operational database
databases.description: MongoDB Atlas Vector Search lets you store embeddings alongside operational JSON documents and perform approximate nearest-neighbor similarity search using the $vectorSearch aggregation stage. It supports hybrid search combining vector, full-text, and metadata filtering, making it well-suited for RAG on live application data.
databases.vector_search_notes: Native. Vector search is built into Atlas via dedicated vector search indexes (HNSW) and the $vectorSearch operator, running alongside document data without a separate system.
databases.llm_integration: No hosted LLMs; integrates with external providers (OpenAI, Anthropic, Cohere, Vertex, etc.) and frameworks like LangChain and LlamaIndex for embedding generation and RAG pipelines.
databases.pricing_notes: Part of Atlas; vector search runs on dedicated Search Nodes billed by instance size/compute and storage, in addition to the Atlas cluster cost; embedding/LLM API usage billed by the external provider.
